summary:
[TO PATRICE DUVICJ 

 


We miss you. More and more terrible and weird things have continued to happen here since you left, but all of us are alive and well and living in Fuller­ ton. Singly and collectively we have phased in and out of sanity, and have discov­ ered that anything is possible. That is to say, anything can happen. We stand amazed but convinced, while trying to love each other as best we can. I feel very close right now to my friends here. It is as if a terrible continual discovery pro­ cess, a confrontation, has been going on between us, which no one planned for or wants or enjoys but from which we all benefit. It is hard to be more specific; so much has happened. Linda Levy has come over a lot. We don’t see Mary, which I think is good. It is also good, very good, to see Linda so much because she is expressing for the first time very deep feelings which she had apparently had all the months I’ve known her but never expressed before. It is as if an inner, deeper, guarded life is emerging finally. What she is saying confirms—at this late date—much of what I believed and felt about both her intrinsically and about what was taking place between us all this time. She can now give an account of everything that happened to us over the months that makes sense emotionally. Evidently she did understand. Why she never said before I don’t know except perhaps she felt fear. Now, with Tessa here, Linda is not afraid of 

76  me or of whatever blocked and inhibited her before...
